metadata.description: Entity relationship graph for CU Entrepreneurship programs and resources

programs.name: Deming Center for Entrepreneurship
programs.description: One-stop shop for students, staff, faculty and community members interested in entrepreneurship. Provides courses, mentorship, funding, and community.

programs.name: New Venture Challenge (NVC)
programs.description: Competition with cash prizes up to $325,000 supporting the pathway from beginning through growth stages. Open to all CU students.

programs.name: Venture Partners at CU Boulder
programs.description: Campus-wide resource for both existing and aspiring university-originated startups seeking non-dilutive funding and support.

programs.name: Catalyze CU
programs.description: An accelerator helping to launch and grow the University's best start-ups. Open to students, staff and alumni.

programs.name: ATLAS Institute
programs.description: Home to research and academic programs transcending disciplinary structures of engineering, design, art, technology and entrepreneurship.

programs.name: Ascent Deep Tech Accelerator
programs.description: A startup accelerator for research teams building deep tech startups coming out of CU campuses.

programs.name: Entrepreneurial Law Clinic
programs.description: Offering valuable legal services to local startup businesses lacking access to legal resources without charge.

programs.name: Idea Forge
programs.parent_organization: College of Engineering and Applied Science
programs.description: A cross-disciplinary prototyping facility where students can design, build and test solutions to meet human needs.

programs.name: Boulder Venture Club
programs.description: A student club designed to be a community and home for students interested in venture capital, startups and entrepreneurship.

programs.name: Embark Deep Tech Startup Creator
programs.description: A deep tech startup creator matching entrepreneurs with university-owned innovations.

programs.name: Get Seed Funding
programs.description: A micro-funding opportunity for undergraduate and graduate students providing up to $500 in funding.

programs.name: Center for Translational Research (CTR)
programs.description: Bridges research and commercial development by connecting university research with industry partners.

programs.name: Lab Venture Challenge (LVC)
programs.description: Pitch competition for university research teams to commercialize their lab findings.

programs.name: NSF I-Corps Hub: West
programs.description: National Science Foundation program supporting innovation teams with training, funding, and resources to commercialize research.

programs.name: Destination Startup
programs.description: Program helping researchers and entrepreneurs relocate to Boulder and Colorado to build their startups.

entities.name: College of Engineering & Applied Science
entities.role: Houses Catalyze CU, ATLAS Institute, Idea Forge

entities.name: Venture Partners at CU Boulder
entities.role: Umbrella organization for deep tech programs

entities.name: IP Support
entities.description: Legal, patent, and intellectual property services

entities.name: Mentorship and Advising
entities.description: Expert guidance from industry and academic mentors

entities.name: Funding and Financing
entities.description: Capital access from competitions, grants, and investments

entities.name: Prototyping
entities.description: Tools, facilities, and expertise for building prototypes

entities.name: Team Building and Networking
entities.description: Community and connections with peers, mentors, and investors

discovered_relationships.title: Venture Partners as Ecosystem Hub
discovered_relationships.description: Venture Partners at CU Boulder functions as the central hub connecting six complementary deep tech programs: Ascent Deep Tech Accelerator, Lab Venture Challenge, Embark Deep Tech, Center for Translational Research, NSF I-Corps Hub: West, and Destination Startup. This creates a comprehensive ecosystem for research commercialization.
discovered_relationships.implication: Entrepreneurs in deep tech should explore all Venture Partners sub-programs as integrated offerings rather than isolated resources.

discovered_relationships.title: Stage-Based Progression Pathway
discovered_relationships.description: A clear progression emerges from early-stage (Get Seed Funding, Deming, Idea Forge) to growth-stage (NVC, Catalyze, Ascent) to scaling-stage (Venture Partners, Lab Venture Challenge) programs. The pathway allows entrepreneurs to graduate through increasingly intense support levels.
discovered_relationships.implication: New entrepreneurs should start with Get Seed Funding + Deming Center, then progress to accelerators and competitions, finally accessing deep tech resources through Venture Partners.

discovered_relationships.title: Research-to-Startup Pipeline
discovered_relationships.description: Four programs work together to convert university research into commercial ventures: Center for Translational Research (identifies research), Embark Deep Tech (matches with entrepreneurs), Lab Venture Challenge (funds commercialization), and Ascent Deep Tech (accelerates growth). This creates a direct path from lab discovery to market.
discovered_relationships.implication: Faculty and PhD students with research innovations should route through CTR → Embark → LVC → Ascent sequence rather than traditional entrepreneurship pathways.

discovered_relationships.title: Support Services Layer Across All Programs
discovered_relationships.description: Entrepreneurial Law Clinic, Idea Forge, and Boulder Venture Club operate as support services that complement ALL other programs. Legal support is needed by all startups; prototyping is needed by hardware/product companies; networking is valuable for all founders.
discovered_relationships.implication: These support services should be layered into any program pathway - they're not alternatives but complements that enhance other offerings.

discovered_relationships.title: Sector-Specific Clustering
discovered_relationships.description: Deep tech sectors (AI/ML, Biotech, Hardware, Aerospace) are served by specialized clusters: Catalyze CU + Ascent Deep Tech for hardware; Lab Venture Challenge + Venture Partners for biotech; NSF I-Corps for broad deep tech. This allows targeted support based on technology type.
discovered_relationships.implication: Entrepreneurs should identify their sector first, then select the cluster that specializes in that area rather than trying all generalist programs.
